Title: Record an encounter and its procedures at the chair
Description: The walk-in loop dead-ends after registration. A doctor must be able to open a patient, start a visit, and add procedures from the catalogue with the doctor attributed. This is the record every downstream thing reads: billing, payout, inventory, history. CLIN-01, CLIN-02.

Title: Interactive invoice builder
Description: The invoice screen is read-only. Build one from performed procedures, with line discount, reason code and an approval threshold. The tax engine is done and tested — this is the human finally driving it. BIL-02.

Title: Take a payment with live allocation preview
Description: Record a receipt across any mode and show, before saving, exactly which invoices it will clear and what becomes an advance. The allocation engine exists; front desk needs to see its reasoning, not trust it blindly. BIL-05.

Title: Close the day for real
Description: The day-close screen renders a reconciliation but cannot lock. Needs the counted-cash entry, mandatory variance reason above tolerance, the lock itself, and an owner-only audited reopen. FIN-01.

Title: Share receipt and ledger statement on WhatsApp
Description: A patient statement they can keep, sent where Indian patients actually read things. Closes the loop on a visit without printing anything. BIL-06.

Title: Swap the in-memory seed for real Drizzle queries
Description: src/lib/seed.ts is a dev scaffold on globalThis. Every read becomes a query against the real schema. Shapes already mirror the tables so this is mechanical, but it is the gate to everything multi-user.

Title: Auth, sessions and RBAC enforcement
Description: Behind our own interface so Supabase stays swappable. Owner, Branch Manager, Front Desk, Doctor, Associate, Assistant, Accountant, Auditor — grantable per branch. Nothing is multi-user until this lands. PLAT-02, ADR-003.

Title: Field-level permissions on financial data
Description: An associate sees their own production and payout, never the branch P&L or another doctor's numbers. Enforced in the data layer, not the UI. PLAT-03.

Title: Tenant isolation enforced in the data-access layer
Description: A cross-tenant read must be structurally impossible rather than a matter of query discipline, and covered by automated tests. NFR-05.

Title: Appointment calendar UI
Description: The scheduling model exists; there is no calendar. Day, week and chair-column views, drag to reschedule, colour by status, visiting-specialist availability across branches. SCH-01, SCH-02, SCH-03.

Title: Patient journey states with timestamps
Description: Booked, confirmed, arrived, in chair, completed. Produces wait-time and chair-time analytics with no extra data entry, which is the only way that data ever gets collected. SCH-04.

Title: Append-only audit log with an in-app viewer
Description: Every financial and clinical write, queryable by Owner and Auditor. Exists in the schema, needs writing to and reading from. PLAT-04.

Title: Import wizard with dry-run and rollback
Description: Every account Anshul closes is switching from Practo Ray, Bestosys, Excel or paper. A migration that goes wrong loses a reference account permanently. Mapping UI, preview, duplicate detection, rollback. PLAT-07.

Title: Free full data export, advertised openly
Description: Patients, treatments, images, ledgers, any time, no charge. Say it in the sales conversation. The moat is trust, not lock-in. PLAT-08.

Title: Invoice PDF with clinic branding and payment QR
Description: Logo, registration numbers, doctor name and council registration, branch address, terms. BIL-12.

Title: Credit notes, refunds and write-offs
Description: Each requires a reason code and role-gated approval, permanently visible in the ledger and audit log. The three ways money leaves without a patient paying. BIL-09.

Title: Instalment schedules and the collections worklist
Description: Due dates, overdue flagging, worklist sorted by ageing bucket. Ortho and implants are collected in instalments and currently nothing tracks them. BIL-08.

Title: Doctor payout engine
Description: Percentage of collection or billing, flat per session or day, per procedure, minimum guarantee. Net of lab, consumables or discount. Rules versioned by effective date; a run is an immutable snapshot so March's edit cannot restate January. FIN-03.

Title: Self-serve payout statements for associates
Description: Every procedure, patient, date, amount collected, deductions, resulting share. The feature that ends the monthly payout argument. FIN-04.

Title: Expense capture by branch cost centre
Description: Rent, salaries, lab, consumables, utilities, marketing. Vendor master, bill photo, approval above threshold. FIN-06.

Title: Branch P&L with drill-through
Description: Revenue, direct costs, operating costs, contribution, per branch per month. Every figure clicks through to the transactions behind it. FIN-07, ANA-06.

Title: Tally export against a mapped chart of accounts
Description: The accountant imports rather than re-keys. The default accounting software in this segment; without this the CA becomes a blocker. FIN-10.

Title: Odontogram with FDI notation
Description: Interactive chart, permanent and primary dentition, per-surface, three toggleable layers: existing, planned, completed. Full-mouth in under three minutes, a quadrant in under thirty seconds, on a tablet with gloves on. That target is an acceptance criterion. DEN-01, DEN-02, DEN-11.

Title: Periodontal charting
Description: Six-point probing, recession, attachment level, bleeding on probing, mobility, furcation, with the previous exam alongside so change is visible rather than remembered. DEN-03.

Title: Treatment planning with conversion tracking
Description: Build from the chart, group into sittings, price from the branch list. Track value presented, accepted, delivered, outstanding. Most practices have no idea what proportion of recommended treatment actually happens. TXP-01, TXP-04.

Title: Lab work orders and bill reconciliation
Description: Order with tooth numbers, shade, material and instructions. Dispatch, receipt, try-in, fit. Promised against actual date. Then reconcile the lab's monthly bill against cases actually received — the part every practice wants and nobody has. DEN-08.

Title: Block a fit appointment when the lab case has not arrived
Description: A burned appointment and an annoyed patient, prevented by a constraint rather than a reminder. DEN-09.

Title: Implant register with batch traceability
Description: Fixture system, lot number, dimensions, site, abutment, prosthesis, review schedule, warranty. Clinical safety and recall requirement, not merely a stock feature. DEN-05, INV-06.

Title: Imaging: RVG, OPG and intraoral capture
Description: Store against tooth and visit, side-by-side and timeline comparison, annotation. Survey what hardware target clinics actually have first — it decides DICOM versus a TWAIN bridge. DEN-07, BRD Q6.

Title: Consumables inventory with automatic consumption
Description: Deduct against the procedure's bill-of-materials on completion, with manual override. This is what turns inventory from a chore into a leakage control. INV-01, INV-03.

Title: Digital consent with versioned templates
Description: Extraction, RCT, implant, ortho, anaesthesia, paediatric, cosmetic. On-screen signature, timestamp, and immutable storage of the exact document signed. CLIN-05, DEN-10.

Title: Prescriptions with formulary and allergy checking
Description: Dose and duration presets, drug-allergy check against patient alerts, layout carrying the prescriber's name and council registration as a valid prescription requires. CLIN-04.

Title: WhatsApp engagement engine
Description: Booking confirmation, 24-hour and 2-hour reminders, post-visit follow-up, balance reminder, recall, payment link. Utility templates are free inside the 24-hour window and cheap outside it; marketing templates cost roughly 0.86 rupees each. Category discipline is a cost decision as much as a compliance one. COM-01, COM-02.

Title: Per-tenant messaging wallet and cost meter
Description: Spend visible by template and branch, configurable monthly cap. Message cost is a real per-account variable cost and must never be silently absorbed. COM-03.

Title: Three-touchpoint confirmation with one-tap reply
Description: At booking, 24 hours before, 2 hours before, each writing straight back to appointment status. Industry reporting puts systematic confirmation at roughly a 40 percent no-show reduction. COM-05.

Title: Recall engine driven by clinical events
Description: Six-month prophylaxis, implant reviews, ortho adjustments, post-op checks — generated from what actually happened, not from someone maintaining a list. Recall revenue is the recurring revenue in a dental practice and most of it is lost to forgetting. COM-06.

Title: Missed-call capture to WhatsApp callback
Description: A missed call at an Indian clinic is a lost patient. Detect it, fire a WhatsApp message with a booking link, log it as a lead. US practices buy voice AI receptionists for this; WhatsApp does the same job for a fraction of the cost and is where Indian patients already are.

Title: Pre-visit digital intake by QR
Description: A code at reception opens the medical history and consent form on the patient's own phone, flowing straight into the record. Takes registration below the 40-second target by moving most of it off the front desk entirely. PORT-03.

Title: Inactive patient reactivation campaigns
Description: Segment by last visit, treatment history and outstanding balance. Every practice has hundreds of patients who simply stopped coming for no reason. Marketing-consent gated. COM-07.

Title: Per-purpose consent register
Description: Treatment, data processing, marketing, image use. Timestamp, notice version shown, channel. Opt-out honoured immediately across every channel. The mechanism DPDP compliance reads from. PAT-08, COM-09.

Title: Patient portal, clinic-branded
Description: Appointments, treatment plan progress, ledger, invoices, prescriptions. OTP auth, no app download. Carries the clinic's branding, never ours — the relationship is with their dentist. PORT-01, PORT-05.

Title: Online booking widget
Description: Embeddable on the clinic site and reachable from a WhatsApp link, exposing only the slot types the clinic chooses. SCH-07.

Title: Owner dashboard across all branches
Description: Collections, billings, new versus returning, chair utilisation, ageing, contribution — every branch side by side. The Sunday-evening screen. ANA-01.

Title: Leakage panel
Description: Unbilled procedures, discounts above policy, ageing, no-shows, stock variance, overdue lab cases, in one place. This is the screen the sales motion demonstrates. ANA-03.

Title: Chair-hour profitability
Description: Which chair earns least per hour, and which doctor is profitable after lab and materials. A differentiating report no incumbent produces well, and impossible without modelling the chair as a resource. FIN-08.

Title: Referral attribution through to revenue
Description: Which referring doctor, campaign or listing actually produces paying patients, not which one feels like it does. Captured at registration, followed to the ledger. ANA-04.

Title: Conversational analytics
Description: Ask the practice data a question in plain language: what did Kothrud collect last Tuesday, which procedures did Dr Rao do most this month. Leading US platforms ship this now and it suits an owner who will never learn a report builder.

Title: Ambient voice charting
Description: Dictate clinical findings and have them land as structured chart entries. Must work in Indian-accented English and Hindi-English code-switching, which is exactly where US tools fail and where we can be better. Depends on the odontogram existing first.

Title: Predictive no-show scoring
Description: Score each appointment on history, lead time, procedure type and payment status, then suggest overbooking or an extra confirmation touch. Cheap to build once a year of data exists; worthless before that.

Title: UPI and card settlement auto-reconciliation
Description: Fetch settlement statements, auto-match to receipts, surface unmatched in both directions, account for MDR and timing so bank credits tie to clinic receipts. The half of the day-book close we have not solved. FIN-02.

Title: Lab-facing portal
Description: Give the dental lab its own view of incoming work orders, due dates and dispatch. Labs touch every clinic in a city and have their own reason to want this, which makes it a second sales channel rather than only a feature.

Title: Treatment plan as a WhatsApp document with one-tap acceptance
Description: Send the plan where the patient will read it, capture acceptance, decline or defer per line, and follow up on what was not accepted. Conversion is the highest-leverage number in a dental practice. TXP-03.

Title: Free leakage audit as the sales motion
Description: Import a prospect's last quarter and show them, in rupees, what was done but never billed, what is ageing, where discounts drifted. Sells the product by doing its job, and doubles as a migration rehearsal.

Title: GST working papers and returns pack
Description: Outward supply register split exempt and taxable, HSN/SAC summary, ITC apportionment where inputs serve both. The pack the CA actually files from. FIN-09.

Title: Confirm the GST treatment with a practising CA
Description: BLOCKING any customer-facing claim. Implant and cosmetic boundaries, ITC apportionment approach. Encoded from public sources today. The highest-damage error available to us. BRD Q5.

Title: Financial-year close pack
Description: Locked period, trial data for the CA, numbering continuity, carry-forward of patient balances and unearned revenue. Year-end is when this product is judged. FIN-13.

Title: ABHA capture and verification
Description: Create or verify an ABHA at registration, QR scan-and-share at the front desk, care-context linking. ABDM milestone M1. PAT-07.

Title: ABDM M2 and M3: serve and consume health records
Description: FHIR R4 bundles against NRCeS profiles, Fidelius encryption, consent handling. The hard part is the FHIR mapping, not the transport. Budget a quarter, not a sprint. Coded diagnoses are already reserved in the schema.

Title: DPDP data-principal rights workflow
Description: Access, correction, erasure and grievance, exposed through the portal with an admin queue and SLA tracking. Substantive obligations commence around May 2027. PORT-04.

Title: Record retention policy per record class
Description: Reconcile the three-year statutory floor with DPDP erasure duties. They pull in opposite directions and the resolution belongs in explicit configuration, not in someone's head.

Title: Sterilisation and instrument traceability
Description: Autoclave cycle records with load contents, parameters and operator; instrument tray traced to the patient. Infection-control expectation under state Clinical Establishments registration. CLIN-08.

Title: Offline tolerance for the front desk
Description: Appointment view and patient lookup readable from cache; receipt entry queues locally and syncs on reconnect. Clinic internet is not office internet. Full offline-first is explicitly not the goal. NFR-02.

Title: Installable PWA
Description: Home-screen icon, full screen, service-worker caching. Probably answers the native-app question entirely, and is a prerequisite for chairside tablet use. ADR-001.

Title: Public REST API and webhooks
Description: Chain-specific tooling and partner integrations. Also the discipline that keeps the specialty-pack boundaries honest. Leading platforms compete on their integration ecosystem now.

Title: Internal ops console for support
Description: A purpose-built view of a clinic's day book, ledger and recent errors. We gave up the free Django admin when we chose TypeScript; this is the honest cost of that, and pretending otherwise makes support unworkable. ADR-001.

Title: Annual VAPT by a CERT-In empanelled agency
Description: Precondition for ABDM production access, and a question every chain owner will eventually ask. NFR-10.

Title: Point-in-time recovery, tested quarterly
Description: Max 15 minutes data loss, restore under 4 hours. Tested, not assumed — an untested backup is not a backup. NFR-06.

Title: Aesthetics and dermatology pack
Description: Packages and courses drawn down per session, memberships, standardised before-and-after imaging with separate clinical and marketing consent, injectable batch tracking, patch-test intervals, deposits. Reuses the unearned-revenue machinery already built. Proof the modular architecture was real. AES-01 to AES-07.
